tool.name: Rerank candidates with a cross-encoder
tool.description: pick the best knowledge-base entry for every entity with a Hugging Face reranker

param.name: input
param.label: Paragraphs with candidates
param.help: JSON Lines, one object per paragraph, with a "spans" list. Every span needs a description and a list of candidate ids, for example from the embedding search step.

param.name: metadata
param.label: Knowledge-base metadata (JSON Lines)
param.help: The same file that was used for the search, for example topostext_metadata.jsonl. It gives the text of every candidate.

param.name: reranker_model
param.label: Reranker model
param.help: Any cross-encoder on Hugging Face that sentence-transformers can load, for example Qwen/Qwen3-Reranker-0.6B or cross-encoder/ms-marco-MiniLM-L6-v2. Bigger models are better but much slower on a CPU.

validator.message: Use the form owner/name, for example Qwen/Qwen3-Reranker-0.6B.

param.name: id_field
param.label: ID field in the metadata
param.help: The field that identifies an entry. Leave empty to use the line number (starting at 0), as the search step does when its ID field is empty.

validator.message: Use letters, digits, dots, dashes and underscores only.

param.name: title_field
param.label: Title field in the metadata
param.help: The text of a candidate is its title, then a colon, then its description.

validator.message: Use letters, digits, dots, dashes and underscores only.
Use letters, digits, dots, dashes and underscores only.

param.name: query_source
param.label: Text to match against the candidates
param.option: The mention itself (the characters from start to end)
A field of the span, for example a description written by an LLM

validator.message: Use letters, digits, dots, dashes and underscores only.

param.name: candidates_field
param.label: Span field with the candidate ids
param.help: The search step writes the candidates as "index_results".

param.name: dtype
param.label: Numeric precision of the model
param.help: float32 is usually much faster on a CPU. Models are mostly saved in half precision, which needs half the memory: choose that for very large models.

param.name: batch_size
param.label: Pairs per batch
param.help: Larger batches are faster but need more memory.

tool.help:
**Rerank candidates with a cross-encoder** chooses, for every entity, the best of several candidate entries of a knowledge base. A cross-encoder reads the mention of the entity and each candidate together, so it is more exact than the vector search that found the candidates. It is the last matching step of the `T4.5.2 Geotagging of texts <https://github.com/atrium-research/T4.5.2_Geotagging_of_texts>`_ workflow.
Input -----
* **Paragraphs with candidates**: JSON Lines, for example from the embedding search step::
{"text": "He sailed to Delphi.", "spans": [{"start": 14, "end": 20, "label": "PLACE", "index_results": ["OLY", "DEL"]}]}
The mention is the text from ``start`` to ``end``. Alternatively, match a field of the span, such as a short description of the entity written by an LLM step.
* **Metadata**: the knowledge-base file of the search step. The candidate ids of a span are looked up in it, and the text of a candidate is its title, a colon and its description. * **Reranker model**: any cross-encoder on Hugging Face that sentence-transformers can load. The tool does not run code from the model repository, so models that ask for custom code cannot be used.
Output ------
The same JSON Lines, with two fields added to every span:
* ``reranker_results``: the id of the best candidate, or ``null`` if the span had no candidates. * ``reranker_scores``: ``{"id", "score"}`` for every candidate, best first. The scores depend on the model and are only comparable between candidates of the same span.
Galaxy has no JSON Lines datatype, so the file is labelled ``json``.
Every candidate of every entity is one run of the model. A small model such as Qwen3-Reranker-0.6B takes a few tenths of a second per pair on a CPU, and a 4B model several times more. The model is downloaded when the job runs, so the server needs internet access.
